sections.title: Differential Equations
sections.description: Analytical methods for formulating and solving first-order and higher-order Ordinary Differential Equations (ODEs) and Partial Differential Equations (PDEs).

formulas.category: Integrating Factor (IF) for Linear First-Order ODE
equations: Used to solve equations of the standard form: dy/dx + P*y = Q, where P and Q are functions of x only.

results: With Constant Coefficients: The complete solution is the sum of the Complementary Function (CF) found via the auxiliary equation, and the Particular Integral (PI).
Cauchy-Euler Equation (Variable Coefficients): Transformed into a linear ODE with constant coefficients by substituting x = e^z or z = log(x).

sections.title: Complex Variables
sections.description: The calculus of complex functions, focusing on analyticity, complex integration, and power series expansions.

equations: The necessary mathematical conditions for a complex function f(z) = u(x,y) + iv(x,y) to be analytic at a point.

key_concepts.explanation: If a complex function f(z) is analytic everywhere strictly inside and on a simple closed contour C, then the contour integral of f(z) along C is exactly zero.

A powerful analytical tool to evaluate complex contour integrals. It states that the integral of f(z) over a closed contour is equal to 2 * pi * i multiplied by the sum of the residues at the isolated singularities (poles) located strictly inside the contour.

sections.title: Probability and Statistics
sections.description: The mathematical foundation for modeling uncertainty, analyzing random variables, evaluating probability distributions, and performing statistical inference.

equations: Used for calculating reverse conditional probabilities—updating the probability of an event (A) based on new evidence (B).

results: Binomial Distribution: A discrete distribution applicable when there are exactly two mutually exclusive outcomes (success or failure) in a fixed number of independent trials.
Poisson Distribution: A discrete distribution representing the probability of a given number of rare events occurring within a fixed interval of time or space.

Normal (Gaussian) Distribution: A continuous, symmetric, bell-shaped distribution completely defined by its mean (mu) and variance (sigma^2). Highly prevalent in natural and engineering processes due to the Central Limit Theorem.
